answer: Rate-metering ties each agent to a scarce, externally verified resource budget, so influence must squeeze through a narrow inlet rather than spill across a wide-open meadow. No velvet rope of curated trust is needed: every identity has to burn metered compute per action, and the meter never resets for free. A swarm of N fake agents therefore has to pay N times that throttled cost in real hardware-seconds, so a thousand shadow identities cost a thousandfold, collapsing the economics of faking yourself into a crowd.
